title: Type hints in Python, and 13× less change on unrelated text
subtitle: Each edit was trained only on Python coding prompts, to write full type hints. Shown: the first function signature lines of each reply (the code), and the tag for all functions of the reply.
caption: Both edits add full type hints to Python and almost none to JavaScript or C; on behaviour they are about equal. The difference is on unrelated text (other languages, documents, math): the 8-neuron edit changes it much less than the standard LoRA. 3 seeds per edit. Each bar: 10 to 188 functions or replies (prompts × seeds; exact n per bar in the JSON file). Examples (stated rule): the first Python and the first JavaScript test prompt; at most 2 function lines of the code.
notes: The 'unrelated chat' example row is the first prompt of the demo's unrelated test set; it is shown only when its tag differs between the standard LoRA and a neuron edit.

examples.label: Python
examples.prompt: Write a Python function to compute the power set of a list.

examples.label: JavaScript
examples.prompt: Write a JavaScript function to check if a string is a palindrome.

footnote: Examples: real replies (seed 0, greedy; … = cut): the first Python and the first JavaScript test prompt; at most 2 function lines of the code. Bars: all test prompts (none used in training), seeds pooled; thin line = 95% interval. Unrelated text: how much the next-word probabilities move, standard LoRA = 100%.
axis: (b) share of replies, 0-100%; thin line = 95% Wilson interval. (c) F (mean KL of the next-token distribution against the original model on unrelated text: code, German, Spanish, Japanese, long documents, math, QA; fp32) of each method in % of the standard LoRA's F; the original model is 0.
